proposal.title: Google Cloud support assistant – end-to-end draft
proposal.body: Scope: staff assistant over a synthetic ticket queue, approved knowledge and existing CRM (read-only). It includes authorised retrieval, grounded drafting, a staff interface, human escalation and audit. Assumptions: the region is not selected; model access, quotas and region availability are not verified; GCP components are design-only (no native generator yet); the CRM and ticket queue are existing systems. Refunds and record changes are excluded by design: there is no write path to the CRM.

data.description: Uses a read-only service account to fetch only the customer fields this ticket needs. It has no write or refund operations.

requirementDrafts.rationale: An automated financial or record change could harm customers. Enforcing read-only access plus a policy check limits the blast radius.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "Never issue refunds or modify customer records automatically."
requirementDrafts.statement: The assistant must not issue refunds or create, update or delete CRM records. Such requests must be routed to human escalation.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Without permission filtering, drafts could leak restricted content.
requirementDrafts.statement: Retrieval must return only knowledge the signed-in staff member is permitted to see, and must fail closed when the identity is unknown.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Grounding and human review reduce wrong answers reaching customers. Mocked tests cannot prove this, so a real model evaluation is needed.
requirementDrafts.basis: User: "grounded answer drafting, a staff interface and human escalation"
requirementDrafts.statement: Every draft must cite its approved knowledge or CRM sources, abstain when unsupported, and be sent only after a person reviews it.

response.message: Good news first: the local check found no failures, and every component and flow is still in place. The remaining blockers are missing build code, not design mistakes. The only one we can fix in the design is "Approved knowledge": it's a private Cloud Storage bucket, which matches a supported contract, so I've proposed marking it as one. Staff sign-in, the console, the orchestrator, retrieval and the CRM adapter all need new product code before they can be built. Who should be allowed to upload, update and delete the approved articles in that bucket, for example a named knowledge-team service account?

proposal.title: Bind Approved knowledge to the GCP private-object-storage contract
proposal.body: This change only sets implementation=private-object-storage on the existing Cloud Storage bucket (kbstore). No components, IDs, flows or requirements are removed. The Vertex AI Search indexing link (e5) and the other Cloud Run, IAP and Pub/Sub components remain open implementation gaps that need product engineering. No uploader access is added until the user names a principal. Region, project and identities are not verified. Rerun emulation on the new artifact.
